label: prf:hecke-markov-transition
title: Proof of hecke markov transition
html:
Proof

(i) Direct computation from (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. Since \sigma_i satisfies a quadratic with distinct roots q and -q^{-1}, the spectral projectors are e_\pm = (\sigma_i - \lambda_\mp)/(\lambda_\pm - \lambda_\mp). Substituting \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} gives the stated formulas.

(ii) The element e_+^{(i)} = (\sigma_i + q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1}) acts on the q-eigenspace as the identity and on the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace as zero. In the permutation representation, the q-eigenspace is the in-order subspace (adjacent elements not transposed) and the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace is the transposed subspace. The convex combination K_i = p_+ \cdot \mathrm{id} + p_- \cdot s_i is manifestly stochastic (non-negative entries, rows summing to 1).

This is precisely the Diaconis--Ram construction [diaconis-ram2000]: the systematic-scan Metropolis algorithm on S_n targeting the Mallows measure \pi(\sigma) \propto q^{\mathrm{inv}(\sigma)} has transition operator K = K_1 K_2 \cdots K_{n-1}, a product of Hecke algebra elements.

(iii) The Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) says that the contribution of the rightmost generator \sigma_n separates as the scalar factor z, regardless of the element x \in H_{n-1}(q). This is the memorylessness of a Markov chain: the transition at step n depends only on the crossing type at \sigma_n, not on the history of previous crossings.

(iv) Follows from (iii) by induction: peeling generators from right to left, each factor \hat{V}_i = z a_i + b_i is independent of the remaining product, giving \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i. \square

Limiting behaviour

At q = 1 (classical limit), p_+ = p_- = 1/2 and the chain is a fair random walk on S_n. As q \to \infty (deep-quantum limit), p_+ \to 1 and the chain becomes deterministic: only the symmetric channel survives, recovering the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP). For the substrate value q = q_0, the per-step Shannon entropy H = -p_+\ln p_+ - p_-\ln p_- is close to the maximum \ln 2; the canonical evaluation is given in Chapter 7 (physical observations).
